rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Rental housing providers in Berkeley may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decision-making. This includes refusing to rent, terminating, or charging a higher deposit or rent based on criminal history. Any adverse action based on criminal history requires written notice and an opportunity to respond.
rules.key_value: Criminal history inquiries and use banned; fines $1,000-$10,000 per violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Current and prospective tenants of rental housing in Berkeley, including advertising, application, leasing, tenancy, and family-member additions.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record lives in one unit as their primary residence; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back per BMC 13.76.130 A.9; existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exemptions for lifetime sex offender applicants, public housing/Section 8 properties (limited), owner move-back rental agreements under BMC 13.76.130 A.9, and existing tenants subletting or adding/replacing roommates; owner-occupied 1-3 unit exemption requires owner residence as primary residence.

rules.penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation; civil damages including actual damages or three times one month's rent; punitive damages; attorneys' fees and costs; injunctive relief.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
rules.conflict_note: The page gives only the City Council passage date (April 14, 2020), not the effective date. The ordinance is treated as in force because the Rent Board is administering complaints under it.
